subject: mathematics
title: Tens and units
summary: What each digit in a two-digit number is worth.

lesson.text: Numbers from 10 to 99 have two digits. The place of a digit tells us what it is worth.
Take 34 broom sticks. Tie them in bundles of 10. You get 3 bundles and 4 sticks left over. So 34 is 3 tens and 4 units.

items: The left digit is the tens.
The right digit is the units (ones).

lesson.title: The number 58
steps: 5 is in the tens place, so it is worth 5 tens = 50.
8 is in the units place, so it is worth 8.

lesson.text: Compare the tens first. 61 is bigger than 49 because 6 tens is more than 4 tens. If the tens are the same, compare the units: 47 is bigger than 43.
Money helps: ₦10 notes are tens and ₦1 coins are units. ₦36 is three ₦10 notes and six ₦1 coins.

questions.prompt: In the number 63, what is the 6 worth?
questions.explanation: The 6 is in the tens place, so it is worth 6 tens = 60.

questions.prompt: What number is 4 tens and 9 units?
questions.explanation: 4 tens = 40 and 9 units = 9. 40 + 9 = 49. 94 swaps the digits round.
Compare the tens: 52 has 5 tens, more than any of the others.

questions.prompt: Funmi has three ₦10 notes and four ₦1 coins. How much money does she have?
questions.explanation: Three ₦10 notes are 3 tens = ₦30. Four ₦1 coins are ₦4. ₦30 + ₦4 = ₦34.
